# Autoshop v2 — Implementation Plan

> **Historical planning document.** It captures the design and the measurements
> taken *while V2 was being planned*; much of it shipped, and several details
> changed on the way (masks, the anchored absolute-Kelvin model, the style index
> and the generative sizing all differ from the sketches below). Present-tense
> statements describe the plan, not today's behaviour — for that read
> [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) and the code.

Synthesis of four research reports against the current state (`src/recipe.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`). Evidence tags `[verified]` / `[unverified]` are preserved from the source reports; do not silently promote any `[unverified]` claim to fact.

---

## 1. `EditRecipe` v2 schema changes

The v2 recipe gains **local masks** as a first-class field, keeping every existing global field untouched (the new field defaults to empty, so all current recipes deserialize unchanged). All UI-scale conventions stay in Rust (−100..100 / stops); scale conversions happen only in the XMP writer.

```rust
// src/recipe.rs — add to EditRecipe (after tone_curve, before provenance):
//   #[serde(default)] pub masks: Vec<LocalAdjustment>,
// default = empty Vec ⇒ no <crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections> emitted, recipe v1-compatible.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct LocalAdjustment {
    pub mask: MaskGeometry,        // where it applies
    pub name: String,             // -> crs:CorrectionName / MaskName
    pub amount: f32,              // 0..1 master opacity -> CorrectionAmount + MaskValue
    pub inverted: bool,           // -> crs:MaskInverted

    // SAME UI scale as the global EditRecipe sliders; writer does /100 and /4:
    pub exposure_ev: f32,         // stops    -> LocalExposure2012  (write /4.0)
    pub contrast: f32,            // -100..100 -> LocalContrast2012 (write /100)
    pub highlights: f32,          //           -> LocalHighlights2012
    pub shadows: f32,             //           -> LocalShadows2012
    pub whites: f32,              //           -> LocalWhites2012
    pub blacks: f32,              //           -> LocalBlacks2012
    pub clarity: f32,             //           -> LocalClarity2012
    pub dehaze: f32,              //           -> LocalDehaze
    pub texture: f32,             //           -> LocalTexture
    pub saturation: f32,          //           -> LocalSaturation
    pub temperature: f32,         //  relative -> LocalTemperature (NOT Kelvin)
    pub tint: f32,                //           -> LocalTint
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum MaskGeometry {
    /// -> crs:What="Mask/Gradient"; vector zero->full defines direction + falloff width.
    Linear { zero_x: f32, zero_y: f32, full_x: f32, full_y: f32 },
    /// -> crs:What="Mask/CircularGradient"
    Radial { top: f32, left: f32, bottom: f32, right: f32,
             feather: f32, roundness: f32, flipped: bool },
}
```

Companion changes required by the schema addition (all `[verified]` against current code):

- **`Default`** — add `masks: Vec::new()` to `EditRecipe::default()` so `is_noop()`/round-trip tests still hold.
- **`clamp()`** — extend to clamp each `LocalAdjustment` slider into the same ranges as globals (and `amount` to 0..1, exposure_ev to ±5/whatever local bound is confirmed — see [unverified] §7).
- **Advisor JSON schema** — `edit_recipe_schema()` is strict-mode (`additionalProperties:false`, all props `required`) [verified: `src/advisor/openai.rs:124-149`]. *R23-1 update: that citation is stale — the schema is no longer hand-written in `openai.rs`; it is generated from the control registry in `src/advisor/catalogue.rs` (wire-identical, pinned byte-for-byte), so schema changes go through the registry now.* Adding `masks` requires: append `"masks"` to `required`, add an array schema whose items mirror `LocalAdjustment` + the tagged `MaskGeometry` enum, with **every nested object's props also `required`**. This is a non-trivial, multi-level schema edit, not one line.
- **No other v2 schema additions** are proposed by the reports. Generative retouch (§5) deliberately lives **outside** `EditRecipe` — it returns pixels, not recipe fields — so it adds no recipe fields, only a new module + CLI surface.

## 2. Local gradient masks — XMP write format + render-engine mask math

### 2a. XMP write format

The masks element is a sibling of `<crs:ToneCurvePV2012>`, emitted before `</rdf:Description>` (`src/xmp.rs:116`). Empty `masks` ⇒ emit nothing. Structure is byte-faithful to the user's real sidecar `<library>/Raw/2023/23-06-Cornwall-Raw/DSC08724.xmp` lines 231–281 [verified: file read].

```xml
<crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections>
 <rdf:Seq>
  <rdf:li>
   <rdf:Description
    crs:What="Correction" crs:CorrectionAmount="1" crs:CorrectionActive="true"
    crs:CorrectionName="Autoshop Linear 1"
    crs:CorrectionSyncID="<fresh 32-hex GUID, uppercase, no dashes>"
    crs:LocalExposure="0" crs:LocalHue="0" crs:LocalSaturation="0"
    crs:LocalContrast="0" crs:LocalClarity="0" crs:LocalSharpness="0"
    crs:LocalBrightness="0" crs:LocalToningHue="0" crs:LocalToningSaturation="0"
    crs:LocalExposure2012="-0.075" crs:LocalContrast2012="0"
    crs:LocalHighlights2012="0" crs:LocalShadows2012="0"
    crs:LocalWhites2012="-0.27" crs:LocalBlacks2012="0"
    crs:LocalClarity2012="0" crs:LocalDehaze="0" crs:LocalLuminanceNoise="0"
    crs:LocalMoire="0" crs:LocalDefringe="0" crs:LocalTemperature="0"
    crs:LocalTint="0" crs:LocalTexture="0" crs:LocalGrain="0"
    crs:LocalCurveRefineSaturation="100">
   <crs:CorrectionMasks>
    <rdf:Seq>
     <rdf:li crs:What="Mask/Gradient" crs:MaskActive="true"
      crs:MaskName="Linear Gradient 1" crs:MaskBlendMode="0"
      crs:MaskInverted="false" crs:MaskSyncID="<fresh 32-hex GUID>"
      crs:MaskValue="1"
      crs:ZeroX="0.5" crs:ZeroY="0.35" crs:FullX="0.5" crs:FullY="0.0"/>
    </rdf:Seq>
   </crs:CorrectionMasks>
   </rdf:Description>
  </rdf:li>
  <!-- radial: identical wrapper; mask li swaps What + geometry -->
  <rdf:li> <rdf:Description crs:What="Correction" ... >
   <crs:CorrectionMasks><rdf:Seq>
    <rdf:li crs:What="Mask/CircularGradient" crs:MaskActive="true"
     crs:MaskName="Radial Gradient 1" crs:MaskBlendMode="0"
     crs:MaskInverted="true" crs:MaskSyncID="<fresh GUID>" crs:MaskValue="1"
     crs:Top="0.30" crs:Left="0.35" crs:Bottom="0.70" crs:Right="0.65"
     crs:Feather="0.5" crs:Roundness="0" crs:Flipped="false"/>
   </rdf:Seq></crs:CorrectionMasks>
   </rdf:Description></rdf:li>
 </rdf:Seq>
</crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections>
```

**Load-bearing writer gotchas** [verified unless tagged]:

1. **Two value scales.** Global `Exposure2012` = literal stops; **local** `LocalExposure2012` = **stops/4**. Global sliders = −100..100; **local** = **slider/100** into −1..1. Reusing the global `signed()` formatter is wrong on both scale and forced-sign.
2. **No forced `+` on locals.** File writes `LocalSaturation="-0.2"`, positives bare. Add a separate `local(v)` decimal formatter distinct from the global signed one at `src/xmp.rs:15`.
3. **Full attribute block required.** Emit all 26 `Local*` fields (legacy PV2010 + 2012) with `0` for unused, plus `LocalCurveRefineSaturation="100"`. *R23-1b update: `LocalHue` and `LocalSharpness` left the "unused" set — the recipe grew a per-mask hue rotation and a SIGNED local sharpness, both written and read back on the same ÷100 ↔ ×100 pair as their neighbours. Every sidecar reachable here (the reference block above included) carries `"0"` for those two, so Lightroom's own numeric scale for them is **[unverified]** (see §7 item 10); our round-trip is exact and Lightroom re-renders from its own model, the same stance as local `texture`.* *v0.32.0 update: `LocalHue` LEFT that pair — a controlled export measured its scale at **180** (slider +50 ⇒ `"0.277778"`), so it converts ×180 / ÷180 on the two boundaries and its import gate moved with it. `LocalSharpness` is still on the family scale and still unmeasured.*
4. **GUIDs unique + 32-uppercase-hex, no dashes** (e.g. `E854A9E19853A449BA92FB800AB0CB29`); fresh `CorrectionSyncID` + `MaskSyncID` per emit.
5. **Geometry coords unclamped** — linear Zero/Full may be negative or >1 (`FullY="-0.023755"`); do not clamp.

Field→crs mapping table (UI scale → written scale): `exposure_ev` → `LocalExposure2012` (÷4); `contrast/highlights/shadows/whites/blacks/clarity/dehaze/texture/saturation/temperature/tint` → corresponding `Local*` (÷100); `temperature` is **relative**, not Kelvin.

### 2b. Render-engine mask math

`src/render.rs` currently applies only global LUT + sat/vibrance, **no spatial term** [verified: `src/render.rs:56-65`]. The XMP→Lightroom path renders masks faithfully today; Autoshop's own preview/export shows only the global edit until a compositor lands. The mask compositor computes a per-pixel weight `m ∈ [0,1]`, then applies the local adjustments scaled by `m * amount`:

- **Linear**: project pixel onto the Zero→Full vector; `t = clamp(dot(p−zero, dir)/|dir|², 0, 1)`; weight = `smoothstep(0,1,t)` (reuse existing `smoothstep`, `src/render.rs`). `inverted` ⇒ `1−m`.
- **Radial**: normalized elliptical distance `d` from the bounding-box center/axes; weight = `smoothstep(1, 1−feather, d)` (inside the ellipse → 1). `inverted`/`flipped` toggle inside-vs-outside.

Local adjustments reuse the same per-channel tone math as globals but applied with weight `m`. This is a separate full-buffer pass after the global per-pixel loop.

### 2c. Tasks (ordered)

1. Add `masks` field + `LocalAdjustment` + `MaskGeometry` to `recipe.rs`; update `Default`, `clamp`, round-trip test.
2. Add `local(v)` formatter + `MaskGroupBasedCorrections` emitter to `xmp.rs` (linear first — byte-faithful; radial second — schema-shaped).
3. Add GUID generator (32-hex uppercase).
4. Extend `edit_recipe_schema()` strict-mode JSON schema for `masks`.
5. (Render parity) add linear+radial weight functions + masked-adjustment pass to `render.rs` and `develop_preview`.

### 2d. Acceptance checks

- Empty `masks` ⇒ output XMP byte-identical to v1 (no masks element).
- A recipe with the one-linear template produces XMP that **opens in Lightroom with the gradient visible and adjustable**, values matching (e.g. `LocalWhites2012="-0.27"` ⇒ −27 slider).
- Round-trip JSON test passes with a populated `masks`.
- ~~[unverified — needs a real Lightroom radial sidecar] radial geometry renders correctly~~ — **MET in v0.32.0.** The sidecars arrived (twelve controlled exports) and the geometry is measured end to end: rotated-corner decode, the `k = 1.032` frame affine, the falloff endpoints, the polarity truth table. See §7 item 1 and `xmp::lr_to_engine`.

## 3. Style retrieval — module + index + prompt integration

Replaces the rejected global-bias `style-profile.json` (one mean bias per slider, `eval.rs:167-183` → `config.rs:54-91`) with per-photo k-NN retrieval of the user's own edits on visually similar past shots, framed as **soft, non-binding reference**. Zero new dependencies — pure arithmetic on what `decode_raw` already returns.

### 3a. Feature vector + distance

14-dim f32 vector from `Meta` + `Histogram` [verified: `src/decode.rs:25-61`]: log focal, log ISO, log aperture, time-of-day `[sin,cos]` (hour from EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`), mean luma, clip-black %, clip-white %, color cast R−G & B−G, as-shot WB warmth `ln(wb[0]/wb[2])`, aspect ratio, tonal-spread (luma stddev), portrait flag. z-score the unbounded log/ratio dims (#1,2,3,11) using corpus mean/std stored in the cache header; bounded dims unchanged.

Distance = **weighted Euclidean**, `d² = Σ w_k (q_k−e_k)²`, hand-set weights (scene-type discriminators 1.5; tone/color regime 1.0; time-of-day 0.5). Cosine/Mahalanobis rejected for n≈150 with sound reasoning. [unverified: the specific weight values are a reasoned starting point, not empirically tuned — a 4-line const table, adjustable after eyeballing retrievals.]

### 3b. Module + cache

New `src/style.rs`: `feature_vector(meta,hist) -> [f32;14]`, `Norm{mean,std}`, `StyleExemplar{stem,feat,tag,settings}`, `StyleIndex{version,library_dir,built_at,norm,exemplars}` with `build/load/save/retrieve/render_reference`. Build = one pass over RAW+XMP pairs reusing `find_raws` (`pipeline.rs:117`), `decode_raw` (cheap embedded-preview path, `decode.rs:92-126`), and `parse_user_xmp` verbatim (`eval.rs:38`). Cache = `out/style-index.json` (~80–120 KB). Retrieve k=4 by linear scan (~2100 mults — negligible), with **self-exclusion** dropping any exemplar whose stem == query stem (the eval case).

### 3c. Prompt integration

Insert in `openai.rs::propose` exactly where `calibration` is appended (after line 67, before the `hint` block) [verified: `src/advisor/openai.rs:61-74`]. *R23-1 update: those line numbers predate the prompt rewrite — `propose_instruction` now assembles the request from the `catalogue.rs` registry (Direction first, guardrails after, style reference via `ProposeContext.reference`), and the reference block's strength-aware ceiling/floor wording lives in `src/style.rs::render_reference`.* Block is explicitly **REFERENCE ONLY — do not copy**, lists each exemplar's derived tag (`[tele/bright/midday]`) + its `Some` settings. Plumbing: add a dedicated `reference: Option<&str>` param to `Advisor::propose` (parallel to existing `hint`, `src/advisor/mod.rs:83-91`), default-ignored by heuristic/claude providers. Do **not** reuse the `hint` channel (that's the verifier's revision note).

### 3d. Wiring + retirement

- New `Command::StyleIndex { dir }` in `main.rs` (mirrors `Eval`) → `StyleIndex::build(&dir)?.save(...)`. Becomes the "learn my taste" entrypoint.
- `produce_recipe` (`pipeline.rs:21-39`): after decode, `let refs = StyleIndex::load("out/style-index.json").ok().map(|ix| ix.render_reference(&ix.retrieve(&meta,&hist,4)))`; pass `refs.as_deref()`. Missing index ⇒ `None` ⇒ identical to today.
- Retire `config.rs::load_calibration`/tendency, `eval.rs` `save_profile` block, and `eval --save-profile`; keep `eval` for scoring.
- Forward-compat: `feat` slot can later become a CLIP/DINO embedding (NDIM 512, cosine) with zero retrieval/prompt change — [unverified: CLIP model/dim + Rust `ort`/`candle` path acceptable on the Windows box; deferred until cheap retrieval's content-blindness is shown to hurt via the `eval.rs` MAE harness].

### 3e. Tasks

1. Write `src/style.rs` (feature_vector, Norm, exemplar, index build/load/save/retrieve/render_reference).
2. Add `reference` param to `Advisor::propose` + impls; inject block in `openai.rs`.
3. Add `StyleIndex` subcommand to `main.rs`; wire `produce_recipe`.
4. Retire global-bias mechanism.

### 3f. Acceptance

- `autoshop style-index <dir>` over the ~150-pair corpus builds a versioned JSON in one pass with no full demosaic.
- A query photo returns k=4 plausible same-scene-type exemplars; self-exclusion verified on a corpus member.
- With index present, the vision prompt contains the reference block; absent index ⇒ prompt byte-identical to today.
- `eval.rs` per-field MAE harness runs unchanged for before/after comparison.

## 4. Render v2 — WB-temp / clarity / sharpen / NR formulas + order

Buffer is `Vec<[f32;3]>`, sRGB-gamma ~[0,1], **already white-balanced to as-shot WB** [verified: `src/render.rs:54`; rawler `develop.rs:181-193,230`]. Luma weight Rec.601 `0.299/0.587/0.114` [verified]. Reuse `srgb_to_linear`/`linear_to_srgb`/`smoothstep`/`sample_lut`.

### 4a. White balance (Kelvin + tint → per-channel gains)

Sign: higher K = warmer correction (Lightroom convention) [verified vs `src/xmp.rs:46-54`; exact internal K→gain curve [unverified — Adobe unpublished]]. **Critical:** buffer is already at as-shot WB, so apply the **ratio** of target-WB gains to as-shot gains, else WB is double-counted.

- `kelvin_to_rgb(K)`: Tanner-Helland piecewise fit, clamp 1000–40000, `t=K/100` — **shipped with the cool-side coefficients RESCALED, deliberately not the published ones** (2026-08-06). The published constants leave the branches not meeting at the 6600 K seam (green +1.31 %, blue +0.96 %) and start the cool red branch at 259.7, which the clamp holds flat to 6688 K — an 88 K band in which `wb_gains`' r/b ratio, the eyedropper's whole temperature signal, does not move. Each branch keeps its published EXPONENT and is recalibrated on the seam values; blue is two-point fitted so repairing the top seam does not open one at 1900 K. See `render::kelvin_to_rgb`. **Validated on a real frame (v0.20.0):** the same 61 MP ARW rendered at 6590 K and 6610 K through both engines — the pre-recalibration engine jumps R −0.67 / B −1.11 (8-bit means) across that 20 K step, the recalibrated one moves ≤ 0.10; at 7000 K the recalibration shifts the rendered mean R +1.47 / B +0.97, at 2000 K B −0.98. Comparison sheets were delivered for visual acceptance.
- `tint_green_factor = 1.0 − 0.20*(tint/100)`.
- `wb_gains = (kelvin_to_rgb(as_shot_k) ./ kelvin_to_rgb(target_k))`, apply tint on green, normalize green→1.0 (WB changes color not brightness).
- **`as_shot_k` source — preferred:** invert the daylight model against `Meta.as_shot_wb_coeffs` (1-D K search, ~30 evals) [verified: coeffs at `decode.rs:41,149-157`] — requires threading `&Meta`/coeffs into `render_to_image`/`develop_preview` which today take `(path, recipe)`/`(preview, recipe)` [verified: `render.rs:32,105`] — **signature change**. **Fallback (no signature change):** assume `as_shot_k = 5500.0` (D55) or 6500 (rawler's D65 white point) anchor — the daylight-relative approximation.
- Apply in **linear light** (gains multiplicative on linear): `linear_to_srgb(srgb_to_linear(px[c])*g[c])`.

### 4b. Clarity — large-radius USM on luma, midtone-masked

`amount = clarity/100`; `radius_px = max(round(0.02*min(w,h)), 8)` [unverified: 2% is a tasteful default, not Adobe-published; algorithm (USM) is standard]. Blur luma (separable Gaussian σ≈radius/2), `detail = l − blurred`, midtone weight `m = 1−(2l−1)²`, `new_l = l + amount*detail*m`, re-apply via chroma-preserving ratio `k=new_l/l`.

### 4c. Sharpening — small-radius USM on luma

`amount = sharpening/100` (0..1.5); `σ = clamp(0.0008*min(w,h), 0.7, 2.0)` [unverified: 1px default conventional]. No midtone mask. Same chroma-ratio reapply.

### 4d. Noise reduction — bilateral-lite luma denoise

`t = nr/100`; `σ = 0.5 + 1.5t`; range=0.05; `w_edge = exp(−(detail/range)²)`; `denoised = l + (1 − t*w_edge)*detail`. Separable blur + per-pixel range weight — **reject true 2-D bilateral** (O(N·r²) on 61 MP frames). Luma-only, matches `crs:LuminanceSmoothing`.

Shared `gaussian_kernel`/`gaussian_blur_plane` (separable, 3σ support) serve clarity/sharpen/NR.

### 4e. Order (ACR-style: WB → tone → presence/local → detail)

| # | Op | Space | Rationale |
|---|----|-------|-----------|
| 1 | WB gains | linear | sensor-space; precede tone |
| 2 | Tone LUT (existing) | gamma | now fed WB-corrected pixels |
| 3 | Clarity (large USM, midtone) | gamma | after global tone, before sat |
| 4 | Saturation/vibrance (existing) | gamma | color after luminance structure |
| 5 | Noise reduction | gamma luma | **before** sharpening |
| 6 | Sharpening (small USM) | gamma luma | last; NR-before-sharpen is the ordering that matters most |

Steps 3–6 are separate full-buffer passes (spatial, can't fold into the 1-D LUT). `develop_preview` runs the same ordered passes for WYSIWYG; parallelize with `rayon` over scanlines for full-res.

### 4f. Tasks

1. Add WB module (`kelvin_to_rgb`, `tint_green_factor`, `wb_gains`) + linear-light apply pass; decide `as_shot_k` source (preferred signature change vs fallback anchor).
2. Add shared separable Gaussian.
3. Add `apply_clarity`, `apply_sharpening`, `apply_noise_reduction`.
4. Insert all four into `render_to_image` + `develop_preview` in the order above.

### 4g. Acceptance

- WB: `target_k > as_shot_k` yields R-gain>1, B-gain<1 (warmer) — assert sign on a unit test; `temperature_k=None` ⇒ gains `[1,1,1]` (no-op).
- Clarity/sharpen/NR each no-op at slider 0; visible, non-color-shifting effect at max (chroma ratio preserves hue).
- NR-then-sharpen order verified (swapping visibly re-noises).
- All four are O(N·σ), not O(N·r²); full-res 61 MP export completes in a handful of separable sweeps.
- Validate Tanner-Helland constants against source before shipping [unverified].

## 5. Generative — object removal + full-frame experiment

Calls OpenAI **Images** endpoints (return pixels, not recipes) — a **separate concern** from the existing Responses-API vision advisor (`src/advisor/openai.rs`). New module `src/edit/openai_image.rs`. Both flows use `multipart/form-data` (NOT JSON) [verified: aifreeapi]. gpt-image-* always returns base64 `b64_json` [verified: createEdit/create refs].

### 5a. Chosen model

**Pin `gpt-image-1.5`** for both flows (config field `openai_image_model`, default `gpt-image-1.5`): it fixed the gpt-image-1 "regenerates whole frame" inpainting defect and is cheaper than gpt-image-1 [verified: developers.openai.com guide + community thread]. Use `gpt-image-2` only when >1.6 MP output is needed (gpt-image-1.5 caps at **1536px long edge ≈ 1.6 MP**; gpt-image-2 up to 3840px ≈ 8.3 MP). There is no `chatgpt-image-latest` in the API [unverified — absence in docs].

### 5b. Object removal — `POST /v1/images/edits` with mask

Endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits` [verified]. Fields: `model`, `image`, `mask`, `prompt`, `input_fidelity=high`, `size`, `quality`, `output_format=png`. **Mask = RGBA PNG, transparent (alpha=0) pixels = region to edit**, same WxH/format as image, <50 MB [verified: guide].

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -F "model=gpt-image-1.5" -F "image=@frame.png" -F "mask=@mask.png" \
  -F 'prompt=Remove the trash can on the left. Fill with surrounding pavement and wall, matching lighting and perspective. Do not alter anything else.' \
  -F "input_fidelity=high" -F "size=1024x1024" -F "quality=high" -F "output_format=png"
```

**Critical caveat:** the mask is *guidance, not a hard boundary* — the model jointly rewrites source+mask+prompt, so output is **not pixel-identical outside the mask** [verified: community thread]. Never blind-overwrite the original; keep as a separate artifact, and ideally re-composite only the masked region back onto the source if the rest must stay untouched.

### 5c. Full-frame reinterpret experiment — `/v1/images/edits` **without** mask

`/images/generations` does **not** accept an input image (text-only) [verified] — it cannot reinterpret an existing photo. Use maskless `/images/edits`; `input_fidelity=high` keeps it recognizably the same photo, `low` gives creative freedom [verified: guide + MS Q&A].

```bash
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -F "model=gpt-image-1.5" -F "image=@frame.png" \
  -F 'prompt=Reinterpret as a moody cinematic edit: deepen shadows, warm highlights, keep subject and composition identical.' \
  -F "input_fidelity=high" -F "size=1536x1024" -F "quality=high"
```

### 5d. New CLI surface (clearly labelled destructive / experimental)

- `retouch <raw> --mask <png> --prompt <str> [--out ...]` — object removal (§5b).
- `reimagine <raw> --prompt <str> [--fidelity high|low] [--out ...]` — full-frame experiment (§5c).
- Both write to `out/<stem>.openai-edit.png` (never beside source); parse `data[0].b64_json` → decode → PNG; log `usage.total_tokens`.
- **Labelling:** help text marks both **EXPERIMENTAL / low-res generative re-render — NOT a deliverable master.** Per-image cost ~$0.03–0.05 medium, ~$0.13–0.25 high on gpt-image-1.5 [verified: pricing table].

### 5e. Resolution caveat (load-bearing)

Output is **30–60× lower resolution** than the 61 MP ARW (1.6 MP ≈ 2.6%; even gpt-image-2 ≈ 14%) and is a lossy generative re-render. Unusable as a master; strictly a low-res experiment/preview, consistent with Autoshop's XMP-first model. These are **hard ceilings, not config knobs**. For full-res object removal, the API will not return 61 MP — either upscale (quality loss) or do the actual removal in the RAW pipeline guided by the AI result.

### 5f. Tasks

1. Add `openai_image_model` to `config.rs` (default `gpt-image-1.5`).
2. New `src/edit/openai_image.rs`: multipart builder (`reqwest::multipart`), edit-with-mask + edit-without-mask calls, base64→PNG, usage logging.
3. Add `retouch` + `reimagine` subcommands to `main.rs`, output to `out/`, experimental labels.
4. (Optional, for §5b fidelity) masked-region re-composite onto source.

### 5g. Acceptance

- `retouch` with a real RGBA mask removes the masked object and writes a PNG; logged `usage.total_tokens` is non-zero.
- `reimagine` returns a recognizable restyle at `input_fidelity=high`.
- Output never written beside the source RAW; help text shows experimental/destructive labels.
- Confirm endpoints/model id/field shapes against a **live probe** before relying on them (see §6, §7).

## 6. Build order across all four, with dependencies

**Phase 0 — schema foundation (must land first).**
`EditRecipe` v2 (§1): `masks` field + `LocalAdjustment`/`MaskGeometry`, `Default`, `clamp`, round-trip test. Everything in §2 depends on this; §3/§4/§5 are independent of it but Phase 0 is the smallest, lowest-risk change and unblocks the most. **No live probe.**

**Phase 1 — two independent tracks (parallelizable):**
- **Track A — Render v2 (§4).** Pure-Rust, no external API, no other-track dependency. Land WB (decide as_shot_k source) → shared Gaussian → clarity/sharpen/NR → ordered insertion. **No live probe** (but validate Tanner-Helland constants offline before ship). Highest deterministic value; do early.
- **Track B — Local mask XMP write (§2a–2c).** Depends on Phase 0. Linear first (byte-faithful, verifiable today against the real sidecar), radial second. The render-engine mask compositor (§2b) depends on **both** Phase 0 and the §4 spatial-pass scaffolding (it reuses `smoothstep` and the full-buffer-pass pattern), so sequence §2b **after** §4's passes exist. **Radial needs a real Lightroom sidecar probe** (§7), not an API probe.

**Phase 2 — Style retrieval (§3).** Depends only on existing `decode_raw`/`find_raws`/`parse_user_xmp` + the `Advisor::propose` signature. Independent of Phases 0/1; can run in parallel but is lower-risk to land after Render v2 so the `eval.rs` MAE harness can measure retrieval's effect against a stable renderer. Adds the `reference` param (touches all `Advisor` impls). **No live probe** for the cheap version; CLIP upgrade deferred.

**Phase 3 — Generative (§5).** Fully independent (new module + CLI, no recipe/render coupling). Land last because it is experimental and the only track that **requires a live OpenAI probe** before it can be trusted.

**Steps needing a live OpenAI probe:** only §5 (Generative). Must verify, against the real API with a key: (a) `gpt-image-1.5` model id + `/v1/images/edits` accepts the multipart fields as documented; (b) mask alpha semantics + non-mask-region fidelity behavior; (c) `input_fidelity` accepted on 1.5; (d) response `b64_json` + `usage` shape; (e) the doc-host redirect (`platform→developers.openai.com`) hasn't shifted again. **No live OpenAI probe is needed for §1–§4 or the cheap §3.** §2's outstanding probe is a **Lightroom sidecar** (radial), not an API.

## 7. Consolidated `[unverified]` list (needs a real file/API test)

1. ~~**Radial mask geometry**~~ — **CLOSED 2026-08-19 (v0.32.0), by measurement.** The item asked for the `Mask/CircularGradient` semantics: the box, `Feather`, `Roundness`, `Flipped`, and whether inside-vs-outside is driven by `MaskInverted` or `Flipped`. All of it is now measured on the user's own controlled Lightroom experiment — twelve exports shot for the purpose, plus pixel measurement of the rendered results (evidence archive `~/.claude/plans/r25-materials/lr-experiment/`: `BBOX-DECODE.md`, `ANGLE-MODEL.md`, `probe2/PROBE2-VERDICT.md`, `probe3/PROBE3-ADDENDUM.md`, `probe4/PROBE4-FINAL.md`, which is the settled statement).

   **What the answers are.**
   * **The box is not a bounding box.** `Top/Left/Bottom/Right` are the ROTATED CORNERS of the ellipse's own box in PIXEL space: `X = (R−L)/2·W`, `Y = (B−T)/2·H` **signed**, then `a = X·cosθ + Y·sinθ`, `b = −X·sinθ + Y·cosθ`. Zero free parameters, and the model makes a sign prediction the library confirms 16/16 (`Left > Right` ⇒ `Angle > 0`, `Top > Bottom` ⇒ `Angle < 0`, both impossible; permutation p = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵). The naive reading was wrong by a median factor of 1.84 in axis ratio (p90 4.86, max 40.7) and left 16 of 195 components unreadable. Verified at the pixel on two rendered subjects.
   * **`crs:Angle`'s sign, pivot and MAGNITUDE.** Positive = clockwise on a y-down screen; pivot = the ellipse centre (25 px against 218 px for the frame centre); the rotation happens in PIXEL space, measured 28.554° against the normalised-frame reading's 19.692° — a 27× gap in error, worth up to 11.2° of rendered tilt over the ±44° range real sidecars use. Lightroom canonicalises to `|θ| ≤ 45°` (195/195 rows, and LRTimelapse's author has the ±45° flip on the record). Both XMP directions now carry it.
   * **The frame affine `k = 1.032`.** The mask lives in a frame 1.032× the export, concentric with it — `x_px = W·(k·n − (k−1)/2)`, so the CENTRE moves too. Settled on a hard-edged mask 2799 px from the frame centre: 3 px residual, against 29.6 px for the rival magnitude and 88.4 px for 「the centre stays put」. ~~`W, H` are the exported dimensions (= DNG `DefaultCropSize`)~~ **ERRATUM, R27 Batch-3: the un-rotated SOURCE frame (`DefaultCropSize`), which coincides with the exported dimensions only on an uncropped landscape capture** — see the closure paragraph below.
   * **`Feather` moves BOTH boundaries**, refuting the sourced Adobe-Community claim that it moves only the inner one. The falloff is a cubic smoothstep — the family the engine already used — from `d_in = k(1−f)` to `d_out = k(1+f/2)`; fitted coefficients 0.99 and 0.45 against the law's 1 and ½, chi2/dof 1.52 at zero free parameters against 1.37 at two. The engine's outer edge had been at `d = 1`, i.e. **a 29 % under-sized mask at Feather 50**. **← R27 Batch-8 five-point ladder update (2026-08-19, `batch8-report.md` §5): the smoothstep FORM is confirmed at the quantisation floor (rms 0.0011–0.0050 in α for f ≥ 0.5) and the midpoint law `1 − f/4` survives, but `d_out = 1 + f/2` is REFUTED at the top — measured `d_out` = 1.223/1.402/1.406/1.414 at f = 25/50/75/100 (ellipse-normalised via the frame's own Feather-0 edge, so independent of the `k` question), i.e. it SATURATES at ≈ 1.41 for feather ≥ 50 instead of rising to 1.5; at f = 100 the law is high by ≈ 0.04 in α at every measured ρ. `d_in` is only bracketed (no untouched reference export of that scene). Engine rendering deliberately NOT changed this batch — the saturation rests on one geometry; `batch8-report.md` §7 item 8 names the second-geometry export required first. ~~Amplitude separability PASSES … and the composition law measures as "blend the corrected OUTPUT by α" (`id`) … a now-quantified divergence.~~ **← OVERTURNED same day (R27 Batch-10, `batch10-report.md` §4): the four-amplitude ladder — one identical mask at slider −1/−2/−3/−4 — IDENTIFIES the law as `par` (α scales the SLIDER): `par` self-consistency rms 0.0057 (at the quantum) vs `id` 0.1048 (12×) vs scene-linear 0.1528; a free power on `par` returns p = 0.786 and scores WORSE, so `par` is identified, not fitted. Batch-8's two `id` arguments both fall (its drag comparison was ~2× and its amplitude-ratio test shared one denominator), and its "local −1.00 ≈ global −0.66 EV" is WITHDRAWN with them. Net: this engine's parameter-scaling compositor matches Lightroom's law after all. Batch-10 also measured BOTH feather branches for the first time (`exp_E_ref` unlocked ρ<1): `d_in = 1−f` is REFUTED (measured d_in ≈ 0.79 − 0.94f, NEGATIVE at f = 100 — the inner branch falls faster than any smoothstep with d_in ≥ 0, and one smoothstep does not span both branches), and the `d_out ≈ 1.41` saturation is confirmed on a second, 4.35-aspect off-centre geometry (1.22/1.41/1.42/1.43 vs E's 1.22/1.40/1.41/1.41). So `render.rs:2140`'s `ramp(1−f, 1+f/2, d)` is measured wrong at BOTH endpoints; still deliberately unchanged — it shares the frame-decision surface of `LR_MASK_FRAME_SCALE` (see the L-05 closure below) and a two-branch replacement law needs its own adjudication.**

The radial-uniformity counter-argument DISSOLVES: over one mask's narrow annulus a distortion polynomial is locally indistinguishable from a scale, which is why per-frame "constants" of 0.984–1.032 were seen at all. Item CLOSED.** The stack question resolved itself: neither `candle` nor `ort` — the inference runs in a PYTHON SIDECAR, `python/embed.py`, because that is what already ships on this box (torch 2.8.0+cu128, transformers 5.2.0) and because the repository already has two sidecars with a hardened download-and-refuse discipline to inherit (`denoise.py`'s `_fetch_verified`, imported rather than copied). `onnxruntime` here has no CUDA execution provider at all, which would have made `ort` a CPU-only path.

   **The model: `google/siglip2-base-patch16-384`, 768-dim, HF licence tag `apache-2.0`, revision `f775b65a79762255128c981547af89addcfe0f88`, `model.safetensors` 1,501,968,264 B sha256 `ed72c0ac…`.** Chosen on the LICENCE, not the benchmark: `openai/clip-vit-large-patch14` carries no licence tag on HF at all and its card says 「Any deployed use case of the model - whether commercial or not - is currently out of scope」, which LAION's H/14 card repeats. This is a public repository whose product is being copyright registered, and SigLIP 2 is unambiguously Apache-2.0 while also being the stronger model on every published benchmark.

   **Both halves of 「tolerate both」 are real, and tested.** The vector is `StyleExemplar::embed: Option<Vec<f32>>`; the distance is TWO BLOCKS, `Σ WEIGHTS[i]·(qᵢ−eᵢ)² + W_EMB·(1 − cos)`, never a concatenation — so `W_EMB = 0`, an absent query vector, or an absent exemplar vector each reproduce the previous ranking exactly, and one index may legitimately hold a mix. `CURRENT_INDEX_VERSION` is 5 and v4 is still READ (the embedding block is additive, so a v4 index ranks the way it always did, and bumping must not brick a Style panel for the length of an hour-long rebuild).

   **What is NOT closed, registered here rather than left to be discovered.** `W_EMB = 2.0` is DIMENSIONAL REASONING, not a measurement — the 14-dim weights sum to 14.5 and a cosine distance spans 0..2, so 2.0 puts the two blocks in the same order of magnitude, and that is the whole argument for it. It has never been calibrated against the user's own library, which is the one experiment that could settle it. `AUTOSHOP_STYLE_EMBED_WEIGHT` overrides it and 0 restores the old behaviour. **Close:** build the index both ways over the user's edited library and compare `eval.rs` MAE — the trigger this item originally proposed, now applicable to the tuning rather than to the decision.

11. **`crs:Roundness` / `crs:Midpoint` pixel meaning** — split out of item 1 when that closed (v0.32.0). Their DOMAINS are settled (±100 and 0..100 integer sliders) and both are carried through recipe and sidecar unchanged; what a Roundness of +40 does to the ellipse is unmeasured, and current Lightroom exposes no slider for either on a radial mask. **Close:** a hand-edited preset `.xmp` carrying `Roundness = 100`, exported and rendered — the same route johnrellis used to produce the `Angle = 0` datum in `BBOX-DECODE.md` §5.1.

12. ~~**Crop geometry** — `crs:Crop{Left,Top,Right,Bottom}` read as an axis-aligned rectangle and `crs:CropAngle` taken 1:1 into the engine's clockwise straighten, both `[unverified]` since M1 (`M1_PLAN.md` §8 #9).~~ **CLOSED 2026-08-19 (R27 P3), by measurement, and consumed in code (Batch-3).** Split out of item 1 because it turned out to be the SAME question: the four crop numbers are the two opposite ROTATED CORNERS of the crop rectangle as plain fractions of the un-rotated source frame — **the identical encoding item 1 found for `Mask/CircularGradient`**, one family, two consumers. `X = (R−L)/2·W`, `Y = (B−T)/2·H` signed; `p = X cosθ + Y sinθ`, `q = −X sinθ + Y cosθ`; the exported size is `round(2p) × round(2q)`, transposed for `tiff:Orientation` 5–8. **7/7 photographs pixel-exact, max residual 0.6 px, zero free parameters**, over two signs of `CropAngle`, two orientations and two source aspect ratios; seven rival models miss by 165–987 px, the naive AABB this engine used among them (485 px, 0/7). Four invented corners — the two the encoding does NOT store — land on a frame edge to 0.00 px, and leave it by 12–25 px under the opposite sign, which is an independent dimension-free confirmation of both the encoding and its sign.

    **There is NO `k` on the crop** (global best-fit scale 1.000006) where the mask frame carries `k = 1.032`: same namespace, same corner encoding, different affine. Measured, not assumed, and commented at the code boundary.

    **The sign** is `rot(source → export) = −CropAngle` — Lightroom turns the CONTENT counter-clockwise by a positive `CropAngle`, i.e. the crop BOX clockwise — measured against rendered pixels on six photographs spanning −3.27°…+1.73°, best pair agreeing to 0.0002°, and the rival hypothesis separated by 34× the residual on the WEAKEST row. This also resolves F3's 「sources partially conflict」 verdict: the three code sources agree, and the apparent conflict was a category error between the box view and the content view of one fact.

    **What is still open** (registered, not blocking): `|CropAngle| > 3.27438°` has no witness — the algebra is angle-agnostic but nothing exercises the ±45 region, the `Left > Right` inversion or the ±45 canonicalisation, and **one export at `CropAngle ≈ +35°` with a 2:3 crop rect tests all three in one frame**; `crs:PerspectiveUpright ≠ 0` (one specimen, dimensions exact to 0.49 px but its content transform is 7 % anisotropic, so whether the crop rect is pre- or post-warp is open); `crs:CropConstrainToWarp="1"` combined with a tilt (0 of 13 tilted rows carry it); a pixel-unit `crs:CropUnit`; and where LrC records a USER-APPLIED quarter turn, which is not the same question as the camera-written `tiff:Orientation` and was not investigated. (§2, §4)

13. **The brush ALPHA KERNEL** — new in R27 Batch-4, and the only thing between 「we carry Lightroom's brush masks」 and 「we draw them」. The GEOMETRY is measured and closed: `Mask/Aggregate` is a one-level group of `Mask/Paint` strokes (300/300 children, nesting depth exactly 2, 39 groups); a stroke's `crs:Dabs` is a four-token state machine `r <f>` / `f <f>` / `h <f>` / `d <x> <y>` (22,966 tokens over 382 components, zero malformed); the polyline is ALREADY densified by Lightroom at **0.2000 · r** (15,582 steps, IQR [0.1998, 0.2001], zero pen-lifts), so nothing is interpolated; and the frame is the PLAIN image frame at **k = 1.00001 ± 2e-5**, x by width, y by height, radius in WIDTH units on both axes — **not** the `k = 1.032` concentric frame the radial corners fold through, calibrated against Lightroom's own `crs:pm_*` pixel boxes on 79 spots to sub-pixel. What is NOT in the sidecar, and cannot be: the falloff as a function of hardness (`crs:CenterWeight` / the `h` token) and the per-dab accumulation law. **The file stores the stroke, never the alpha.** The only published model is a third-party decompile reconstruction whose `Density` field does not exist in any of the 382 real components. Until it is measured the geometry is carried and NOT rendered, disclosed by name in both directions (`MaskImportReason::BrushCarried` / `MaskLossReason::BrushCarried`) — the same stance `roundness` is held at, and for the same reason: never reshape a mask on a guess. ~~**Close:** one Lightroom export — three strokes at Feather 0 / 50 / 100 …~~ **← that experiment RAN 2026-08-19 (R27 Batch-8, 16 exports + 5 sidecars, `batch8-report.md`) and pinned FOUR of the six axes while FAILING the one that gates rendering.** PINNED: accumulation is **SCREEN on both axes** (within a stroke and across components — forward-rendering held-out drags from the measured single-click profile predicts α up to 0.93 across 90 dabs with 0.4 % peak error; `max` dead, `sum-clamp` loses 3.2× in bias); **density (`MaskValue`) SCALES the per-dab deposit** (the cap reading refuted at 13× — P4 §7.1's `min(MV,·)` is wrong); dab frame plain-1.0 re-confirmed at 7σ against `k = 1.032`; 0.2000·r spacing replicated with ripple below the 8-bit floor (no anti-ripple needed). Bonus identities: LR's brush **Size is the α = 0.5 diameter** (266.1 ± 5.0 px invariant across the feather ladder while `crs:Radius` = the outer support runs 276→733 px), and `CenterWeight ≠ 1 − Feather/100` (Feather 50 → 0.1621). MARGINAL: kernel shape — best family `(1−ρ²)ⁿ` at rms 0.020–0.022, ~5× the quantisation floor, `n(h)` sampled at 3 points only. **FAILED: flow.** A single dab does NOT deposit `flow·k(ρ)` — refuted model-free (composition-law-independent) at 2.56× and again by the drag ladder at 2.8×; the deposit's SHAPE changes with flow (α = 0.5 radius 209/215/264 px at flow 0.25/0.50/1.00, so not separable as `D(f)·k(ρ)`); three peaks (0.0682/0.1937/0.9930) fit no closed form. Rendering with the naive flow law would be wrong by 3.7× at flow 0.25 — worse than the honest disclosure — so the arm stays CARRIED, per the pre-registered criterion in `batch8-report.md` §6.1. ~~**Close (updated):** `batch8-report.md` §7 item 2 — an 11-rung flow ladder…~~ **← that ladder RAN (R27 Batch-9 synthesised it, Batch-10 measured it) and FLOW IS CLOSED: the deposit is separable `D(f)·k(ρ)` with a one-parameter odds law `D/(1−D) = κ·f/(1−f)`, κ = 0.1219 ± 0.0027** (fit rms 0.0070, held-out 0.0097; `D(1) = 1` exactly, killing the "flow 1.0 different code path" hypothesis; batch-8's non-separability was an `id`-composition artefact plus a zero-point — `batch10-report.md` §3). Screen accumulation and density-scales-the-dab re-confirmed OUT-OF-SAMPLE (a held-out 51-dab stroke carrying density 0.5 AND flow 0.25 predicts at rms 0.0045); 8 of 12 held-out strokes land at/below the 0.0085 quantum. **What still gates rendering, per the §6.1 criterion re-score (`batch10-report.md` §7): (a) the KERNEL — 11 rungs measured but NO closed form exists** (six families; the only one spanning h = 0→1 has parameters discontinuous in h; the measured table interpolates at max 0.0344 = 4× the floor), **and (b) a NEW frame blocker — the mask is rasterised in the PRE-lens-correction frame** (Batch-10 §5), which this engine cannot reproduce (no `.lcp` parser, `crs:LensProfileEnable` never read, our geometry stage uses Sony EXIF knots = a different polynomial). Implementation sketch, ready when the frame decision lands: `batch10-report.md` §7.4 (pre-rasterise the dab group like `Bitmap`/`AiMask`, no schema change; κ + the 11-rung table + held-out residuals as the pinned test values). **Close:** the `LR_MASK_FRAME_SCALE` user decision (§7.5 there), plus either a kernel closed form from denser h sampling or an explicit accept-the-table ruling.

   *R27 Batch-5 widened WHAT is carried without moving this gate an inch.* An AI mask's `crs:Gesture` child — the photographer's brush refinement, 83 of 218 real `Mask/Image` components, exactly one `Mask/Paint` each — is now parsed into `MaskGeometry::AiMask::gesture` through the SAME `parse_paint_stroke` and re-emitted by the same spelling. It is carried and NOT rendered for exactly the reason above: the kernel is not in the file. So the experiment this item asks for now buys two things instead of one, and the count of unrendered stroke geometry it would unlock went up, not down.

14. **`Mask/Image` re-derivation** — 105 instances in the reference library, 78 corrections and 40 files still refused on import after R27 Batch-4, which makes this the DOMINANT remaining term and one no brush work touches. Exhaustive attribute enumeration finds **no raster payload and no geometry payload** (longest attribute value anywhere on one: 55 characters). The sidecar carries the INTENT (`crs:MaskSubType` ∈ {0 = Object/Background, 1 = Subject, 2 = Sky}, `crs:MaskName`, `crs:ReferencePoint`), the PROVENANCE (`crs:ModelVersion` + three digests) and the PROXY GEOMETRY the model ran in (`crs:FullMaskSize` ≈ 2880×1920, `crs:WholeImageArea`, `crs:Origin`) — and nothing else. So this is not a parser item at all: importing these needs a subject/sky/object segmenter of our own producing our own alpha, and its output would be an APPROXIMATION of Adobe's, never a reproduction. The carrier already exists (`MaskGeometry::Bitmap`, which `fit_zoned` already drives for sky), and R27 Batch-4 made the segmentation sidecar's own licences safe to build that on (`python/segment.py`: SegFormer's weights are licensed 「for research or evaluation purposes only」 and were replaced with MIT OneFormer; rembg's default session is pinned so an upstream flip to the pay-to-use `bria-rmbg` cannot land silently). **Close:** point the existing segmentation at the `MaskSubType` the sidecar names, and disclose the result as a re-derivation rather than an import — a DIFFERENT feature from round-tripping, and it must never claim to be one. (F2 anatomy §3, §6 Arm C; D1 §3)

   **LANDED 2026-08-19 (R27 Batch-5), exactly as the close line specifies — and it is a RECOMPUTATION, which is why this item does not read 「closed」 the way a parser item would.** `MaskGeometry::AiMask` carries the measured intent (`subtype`, `ref_x`/`ref_y`, `name`, `mask_version`, the composition triple) plus a `provenance` list holding the eleven attributes this engine never interprets, all of it re-emitted verbatim so a republished sidecar still tells Lightroom which segmentation to run. At DEVELOP time `segment::resolve_ai_masks` runs our own segmenter — subtype 1 → BiRefNet/U²-Net subject, 2 → OneFormer ADE20K sky, **0 → SAM 2.1 Hiera-Large point-prompted at `crs:ReferencePoint`** (new, Apache-2.0, sha256-pinned at revision `665f8e2a…`, 897,897,416 B) — and caches the 8-bit grey alpha (4096 long-edge cap) beside the develop, keyed by photo + subtype + click + backend generation.

   **Measured on the M-B fixture family, before → after:** `_DSC8904` 8/13 → 13/13, `_DSC9082` 3/5 → 5/5, `_DSC9414` 3/5 → 5/5; 33 → 42 masks imported across the seven sidecars, 9 refusals → 0.

   **The disclosure is the load-bearing half and it runs in both directions**: `MaskImportReason::AiMaskRecomputed` / `MaskLossReason::AiMaskRecomputed` (en + zh 「AI 蒙版（本机重算，非 Adobe 原栅格）」), plus a separate `AiMaskUnresolved` for a mask with no alpha at all, because 「approximated」 and 「not drawn」 are not the same news. A sidecar or model failure leaves the mask carried and the adjustment SKIPPED — not rendered at weight 0, which under `inverted` would apply the edit to the whole frame.

   **What is still open.** (a) Object vs BACKGROUND is not decidable from the sidecar — both are `MaskSubType=0`, and `crs:MaskSubCategoryID` appears on 8 of 218 with two values, far too few to call an enum — so the segmenter is pointed at the object under the click in both cases and the possibility is disclosed rather than guessed. (b) HOW CLOSE our alpha is to Adobe's is unmeasured: the honest statement is that the sidecar carries no raster, so the two cannot be compared without a controlled Lightroom export of the same mask. **Close (the remaining half):** export one Lightroom photo with a sky mask, both the sidecar and the developed JPEG, and measure our re-derived alpha against the rendered result — the same shape of experiment items 1 and 13 use.
